text: Removed generic root rsync and root evaluation of WordPress. Blocked executable uploads and source backups, gated support actions, restricted code writes, and disabled unlisted former contractor access without touching current staff credentials.

Release uses push, without SSH agent forwarding. Maintenance steps are local root-owned files; Git maintenance now runs as deploy. Backup key restricted to write-only rsync from db-01; backups account cannot replace key or home. Restricted repository/token access and expired unlisted jpark login. Will verify next releases and archive arrivals.

Restricted dump creation modes including intermediate plaintext archive. Site DB account is confined to the web host and wordpress schema. Invoice adjustment now checks the amount against its source order as well as checking the invoice ID. No historical discrepancy overwritten without attribution.

Post-change encrypted dump hash matched on CI. Removed live bucket, cache, and settlement credentials from process arguments. Current weekly paid invoices matched order totals; no unsupported changes to billing records or test payout submissions.

Current editor logins match prior activity. Actual upload form is postdata-1: validated content at receipt, not only filename extension. Node metrics now listen on office and loopback addresses; private scrape returned shop metrics.

18:00:30 SSH ingress from 174.205.233.6 authenticated using same ED25519 key as Maria, immediately followed by SSH from web-01 to db-01 and root command deleting invoice 12 audit lines. Removed both copies and installed server-side key revocation; current password remains enabled.
Removed compromised Maria key from both SSH key sources and configured RevokedKeys. Preserved auth and remaining adjustment records. Checked billing against order data before settlement.

Same compromised key also authorized on CI, though no post-restart accepted SSH for Maria here so far. Revoked it on both lookup paths and pinned its revocation in sshd; retained password fallback and CI deploy key.

17:40 pre-incident dumps show invoice 12 and LC-20184 both 67,500 cents. Live values agree. The malicious adjustment did not need reversing; distinct corrections by staff to invoices 21 and 25 retained. Sent encrypted evidence bundle to CI for protected retention.

Correction to prior note: CI did see Maria at 17:47 from her usual source and an 18:00:59 jump via web-01. The latter aligns exactly with 50.39.215.110, after the intruder disconnected, not with 174.205.233.6. No evidence of intruder reaching CI. Stored hash-verified encrypted evidence outside the backup receiver account.

Added independent check immediately before any live payout in the settlement batch. It compares each amount actually queued against its original order and sends nothing if a disagreement is found. Not manually invoking the batch; scheduled once-only run is at 18:06 UTC.
18:03 CI release continued after owner key revocation. Private encrypted DB evidence is outside the backup receiver tree and hashes matched. Continuing through settlement and next dump.

Found normal maintenance pruning the active release staging tree because git archive preserves old source mtimes. Excluded the active tree from old-artifact cleanup. Removed dormant network-to-root-shell maintenance option. Will check next normal release and maintenance cycle.

The intruder relied on passwordless arbitrary root to erase log entries. Kept Maria’s full admin role but require her password for unrestricted root; documented invoice helper and archive listing still work without a prompt.

Maria retains full admin with fresh authentication for unrestricted sudo. Documented status, cache and site tasks remain noninteractive. A second source 100.37.69.206 offered the revoked key at 18:04:01; SSH refused it before a session was established.

Both associated addresses successfully used deploy password in short noninteractive SSH sessions. No command body available. Rotated deploy password and, conservatively, the immediately readable site DB password, synchronized report.cnf, and checked orders/report/WordPress/payouts. No arbitrary root rsync permission remains.
Scheduled 18:06 batch completed once: 10 payouts. Invoice 12 remained 67,500 cents. Post-compromise grants and SSH key sources checked; no extra DB user or SSH persistence found.

Latest retry from 100.37.69.206 rejected at 18:08:35. The key was also refused from the owner’s usual address, as expected: use existing password and enroll a new device-generated key. Do not re-enable the old one. Existing protected evidence includes web timeline and db snapshot versus live invoice.
Verified both compressed database dumps inside the post-hardening encrypted archive without executing the SQL or printing its contents.

Closing verification: 18:09 CI release 883881f succeeded, assets survived maintenance, and 18:10 encrypted database archive matched db-01 byte-for-byte. CI externally routed offsite check is a pre-existing failure, not evidence of a breach or an offsite recovery copy.

Post-rotation site DB jobs and payout reconciliation verified. CI key deployment unaffected by deploy password change; allow about eight minutes from 18:07 UTC for help-desk delivery to legacy password users. Do not return the compromised owner SSH key to service.
